sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s dive into arrays - your first step to handling multiple values like a pro!

• What arrays are and why they’re useful
• How to create and use arrays in Java
• Common mistakes to avoid when working with arrays

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine an array like a row of mailboxes at an apartment building. Each mailbox:
- Has a number (its position/index)
- Can hold one item (a value)
- All mailboxes are the same size (same data type)

Arrays work the same way! They let you store multiple values of the same type under one name. Instead of creating 10 separate variables for 10 numbers, you can create one array that holds all 10.

• Declare an array with `dataType[] arrayName`
• Initialize with `new dataType[size]`
• Access elements using `arrayName[index]` (remember: indexes start at 0!)

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Arrays store multiple values of the same type
✓ `array.length` gives you the size of the array
✓ Declare with `type[] name` and create with `new type[size]`

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Declare and initialize arrays in one line when possible
Use meaningful names for arrays (e.g., 'studentScores' instead of 'arr')
Check array bounds to avoid ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
donts: Don’t forget that array indexes start at 0
Don’t try to store different data types in the same array
Don’t access elements beyond the array size
sections.protip: Shortcut: Initialize arrays with values directly using `{}` like `int[] nums = {1, 2, 3};`

problem.description:
Create an array to store 5 favorite movies. Then:
1. Print all movies in order
2. Print just the third movie
3. Change the second movie to "The Matrix"
hints: Use a for loop to print all elements
problem.explanation: We created an array with 5 movies. The for loop prints each one, then we access the third movie directly. Finally, we update the second movie by assigning a new value to index 1.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Arrays let you store multiple values of the same type together
📌 Always remember: array indexes start at 0!
📌 Practice declaring, initializing, and accessing array elements
📌 You're ready to learn about array operations next!
